info.title: ZunoPilot API — mobile surface
info.description:
The endpoints a ZunoPilot mobile client calls.

### Authenticating
Sign in with a phone number and a one-time code: `POST /auth/otp` sends it,
`POST /auth/otp/verify` exchanges it for a JWT. Send that token as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>` on every other request. There are no passwords.

**The token currently lasts 24 hours and there is no refresh endpoint.** A mobile
client will therefore be signed out daily until one is added — worth planning around.

### Shape of a response
Success is always `{ "success": true, "data": … }`. Failure is always
`{ "success": false, "message": "…" }`, with the message written for a person to read.

### Statuses worth knowing
- **401** — no token, or an expired one. Sign in again.
- **403** — signed in, but this seat lacks the permission the route needs.
- **404** — either the thing does not exist, **or** the workspace does not have the
  module that owns it. The two are deliberately indistinguishable, so a workspace
  cannot probe for features it was never sold.
- **422** — WhatsApp refused something, and `message` carries their own words.

### Push notifications
The endpoints under `/notifications/push` are **Web Push (VAPID)**. There is no FCM or
APNs support yet, so a native client cannot receive pushes through them — the in-app
list and unread count under `/notifications` do work.

post.summary: Open a conversation with a customer
post.description: Returns the existing open one if there is one, rather than a duplicate.

delete.description: Needs `inbox:delete`. Soft-removes every message in the conversation. **Messages only** — the conversation, the customer, their orders, the internal notes and any linked ticket all survive, and the thread stays in the list reading as empty. `lastMessageAt` is left alone, so the queue order does not move.

post.description: Needs `inbox:reply`. **422 means WhatsApp refused it** and `message` carries Meta's own words — an expired 24-hour window, a number not on a sandbox allow-list, and so on. 424 means the workspace's WhatsApp token has expired and must be reconnected.

Needs `inbox:reply`. Upload the file first with `POST /media`, then send its id here. **Only within 24 hours of the customer's last message** — outside that window WhatsApp accepts templates only, and this returns 400 saying so. A file a customer sent you cannot be forwarded back; upload your own copy.

delete.summary: Remove a message from the inbox
delete.description: Needs `inbox:delete`. **A soft delete, and not an unsend.** The row survives with `deletedAt` set, so reports and the record of what was said are unaffected — and WhatsApp has no unsend, so the customer keeps their copy regardless. Idempotent: removing an already-removed message answers 404 and keeps the original remover.

post.description: Needs `inbox:assign_self` to take it yourself, `inbox:assign_others` to give it to somebody else. Send `agentId: null` to unassign.

post.summary: Pause or resume the bot on this thread
post.description: Needs `inbox:toggle_automation`. Pausing sets the status to HUMAN_TAKEOVER.
Needs `inbox:add_note`. Never sent to the customer.

post.summary: Hand the thread to a human
Give the thread back to the bot

get.description: Needs `customers:read`. Paged. **`waId` and `phone` come back masked** unless the seat holds `customers:view_full_number` — the masking happens on the server, so the full number is never sent and then hidden.
Needs `orders:read` and the ECOMMERCE module. Paged.
Separate from the list on purpose: the list is paged, so summing its page would report the revenue of fifty orders as the revenue of the business.

patch.description: Needs `orders:write`. Only the transitions the workflow allows are accepted.

get.description: Needs `catalogue:read` and the ECOMMERCE module. What a workspace *calls* its catalogue is on the session as `tenant.catalogueNoun` — a restaurant sees "Menu", a grocery sees "Products".
This user's notifications, newest first. **Never carries a full phone number.**
Cheap enough to poll for a badge.
**Web Push only — not FCM or APNs.** A native client cannot use these yet.

post.description: Needs `tickets:write`. Usually raised from a conversation.

post.summary: Send the customer an update on WhatsApp
post.description: Honours the 24-hour window. If WhatsApp refuses, the text is **still saved on the ticket** and the response says why rather than losing what was written.
What the click-to-dial button records after the call.

bearerAuth.description: The token from `POST /auth/otp/verify`. Currently valid for 24 hours.

BadRequest.description: The request was not acceptable. `message` says why, in plain words.

Unauthorised.description: No token, or an expired one.

Forbidden.description: Signed in, but this seat does not hold the permission this route needs.

NotFound.description: Not found — **or the workspace does not have the module that owns this route.** The two are deliberately the same answer, so a workspace cannot probe for features it was never sold.

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limited. Back off and retry.

WhatsappRefused.description: WhatsApp refused the message, and `message` carries Meta's own explanation — the 24-hour window has closed, the number is not on a sandbox allow-list, a template is unapproved. Not a server fault; show it to the user.

WhatsappDisconnected.description: The workspace's WhatsApp access token has expired or been revoked. Nothing can be sent until an owner reconnects in Settings.

message.example: This conversation is assigned to someone else.

details.description: Field-level problems, when the failure was a validation one

total.description: Rows matching the filter, not rows in this page

Session.description: Everything a client needs on launch.

catalogueNoun.description: What this business calls its catalogue. Use it in the UI.

permissions.description: What this seat may do, e.g. `inbox:reply`. For hiding UI, never for trusting.

modules.description: Which optional modules this workspace has. A missing one 404s its routes.

aiAgentEnabled.description: The workspace half of the AI switch. An operator can revoke the AI_AGENT module above this, and that ceiling cannot be lifted from here.

status.description: Delivery state, from Meta. `RECEIVED` is the inbound default. **Take the state from here, not from the timestamps below** — Meta delivers status webhooks out of order and the server refuses to move a message backwards, so a set `readAt` beside a null `deliveredAt` is normal rather than missing data.

statusError.description: Why Meta refused it, in Meta's own words, with phone numbers scrubbed. Set only alongside `FAILED`.
statusError.example: 131030: Add recipient phone number to recipient list

sentByUserId.description: Null on an OUTBOUND message means the bot sent it, not a person.

waId.description: The WhatsApp number, E.164 digits with no plus. **Masked to `+••••••1234`** unless the seat holds `customers:view_full_number`.

totalPaise.description: Money is always an integer number of paise. Never a float.
